title: Reading Drill — Planning a flood notice route — A pilot study
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Planning a flood notice route — A pilot study
passages.body:
**A** A project in Ravensmere began with reports of warnings reaching uphill streets later than expected. The neighbourhood coordinator had heard several complaints, but individual reports could not show how often the problem occurred. The team collected evidence using delivery logs and chose time to receive a warning as its main measure. That allowed it to compare different days using the same rule.

**B** The proposed response was a fixed order for notice delivery. Rather than apply it immediately across the whole site, the team ran a trial in a single area. The trial lasted ten weeks. A second area kept its previous arrangements, making it possible to see whether any change occurred at both sites.

**C** The first review recorded temporary road closures as a factor that could affect the comparison. The team advised repeating the study under different conditions before drawing a wider conclusion. It kept the evidence from the first trial but published a note about why the figures might not apply elsewhere.
